```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(scales)
library(readxl)
library(writexl)
library(kableExtra)
library(formattable)

# Focus on common big game calibers in Colorado/Western hunting
key_calibers <- c("270 Win", "308 Win", "30-06 Springfield", "6.5 Creedmoor", "300 Win Mag", "300 WSM", "243 Win", "7mm Rem Mag", "7mm-08 Rem")

# Load cleaned dataset
ammo <- readRDS("results/ammo_clean.rds") %>%
  filter(
    !str_detect(coalesce(name, ""), regex("FMJ|Full Metal", ignore_case = TRUE)),
    !str_detect(coalesce(style, ""), regex("FMJ|Full Metal", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  # 1. Unify Bass Pro and Cabela's
  mutate(
    retailer = case_when(
      str_detect(retailer, regex("Bass\\s*Pro|Cabela'?s", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Cabelas/Basspro",
      TRUE ~ retailer
    ),
    dedup_id = coalesce(upc, mpn, name)
  ) %>%
  # 2. Deduplicate by the newly combined retailer entity and product ID
  group_by(retailer, dedup_id) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = date, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(caliber %in% key_calibers)
```

\newpage

## Methods & Data Processing

### Data Collection & Scope
* **Data Sources:** Pricing and catalog data were aggregated across major brick-and-mortar storefronts in Colorado and online retailers shipping directly into the state.
* **Date Range:** Data were collected between `r min(ammo$date)` and `r max(ammo$date)`.
* **Regulation Alignment:** Full Metal Jacket (FMJ), match target ammunition, and solid non-expanding target rounds were filtered out to reflect projectiles legally permitted for big-game harvest under Colorado Parks and Wildlife (CPW) regulations (expanding/mushrooming bullets only).
* **Caliber Focus:** Analysis is restricted to a sampling of popular Colorado big-game centerfire rifle calibers, excluding rimfire, pistol cartridges, and bulk military-surplus chamberings.

### Deduplication & Standardization
* **Product-Level Identity:** Individual listings were deduplicated across retailers using Universal Product Codes (UPC) and Manufacturer Part Numbers (MPN), falling back to title matching where identifiers were unlisted.
* **Temporal Recency:** For retailers with repeat scrapes over time, only the most recent observed price per product was retained.
* **Pricing Unit:** All costs reflect factory loaded ammunition normalized to Price Per Round (USD/rd). Box counts (20-round standard hunting boxes vs. 50-round packages) were standardized by dividing total box price by box quantity prior to aggregation.

## Dataset Overview

```{r overall-summary}
overall_summary <- ammo %>%
  filter(!is.na(ppr), ppr > 0) %>%
  summarise(
    `Total Listings` = n(),
    `Mean PPR`       = mean(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Median PPR`     = median(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Min PPR`        = min(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Max PPR`        = max(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    `IQR PPR`        = IQR(ppr, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

kable(overall_summary, digits = 2, caption = "High-Level Market Summary (USD per Round)")
```

Across all tracked calibers and retailers, the typical price per round sits at `r scales::dollar(overall_summary[["Median PPR"]])` - the median listed above. Because high-end rounds can pull the arithmetic mean upward, this report primarily relies on the **median** (the middle price on the shelf/online) to represent where everyday consumer costs likely sit.

## Price Comparison: Lead vs. Lead-Free

```{r price-summary}
lead_vs_free_summary <- ammo %>%
  filter(!is.na(category), !is.na(caliber), !is.na(ppr)) %>%
  group_by(caliber, category) %>%
  summarise(
    count      = n(),
    median_ppr = median(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_ppr   = mean(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_ppr     = sd(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(caliber, category)

plot_data <- lead_vs_free_summary %>%
  select(caliber, category, median_ppr) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = median_ppr) %>%
  rename(Lead_Core = `Lead-Core`, Lead_Free = `Lead-Free`) %>%
  mutate(
    premium = Lead_Free - Lead_Core,
    caliber = reorder(caliber, Lead_Free)
  )
```

### Median Pricing Dumbbell Chart

```{r dumbbell-plot}
p_dumbbell <- ggplot(plot_data) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = Lead_Core, xend = Lead_Free, y = caliber, yend = caliber),
    color = "#a0a0a0", size = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(x = Lead_Core, y = caliber, color = "Lead-Core"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = Lead_Free, y = caliber, color = "Lead-Free"), size = 3) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = pmax(Lead_Free, Lead_Core, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.1,
      y = caliber,
      label = ifelse(premium >= 0, sprintf("+$%.2f", premium), sprintf("-$%.2f", abs(premium)))
    ),
    hjust = 0, size = 3.5, color = "#2c3e50"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Ammunition Type",
    values = c("Lead-Core" = "#2b5c8f", "Lead-Free" = "#d95f02")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = dollar_format(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Price per Round: Lead-Core vs. Lead-Free",
    subtitle = "Comparing factory ammunition prices across common big game calibers",
    x = "Median Price per Round (USD)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Scraped Retail Ammunition Data From Major Colorado Retailers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#eeeeee", linetype = "dashed"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8)
  )

p_dumbbell
```

**How to read this chart:**

- Each horizontal line represents a single caliber.
- The **blue dot** marks the median price of traditional lead-core rounds.
- The **orange dot** marks the median price of lead-free (copper/monolithic) rounds.
- The grey line between the two dots illustrates the price gap, with the dollar figure at the end indicating the median price difference per round.

**Takeaway:** Lead-free ammunition carries a consistent price surcharge across standard hunting calibers - generally between **+\$0.35 and +\$0.50 per round** (or roughly \$7.00 to \$10.00 more per 20-round box). In magnum cartridges (7mm Rem Mag, 300 Win Mag, 300 WSM), premium lead-core hunting loads approach price parity with lead-free offerings, sitting at a higher initial price per round in general.

\newpage

### Price Table

```{r price-table}
formatted_table <- plot_data %>%
  arrange(desc(Lead_Free)) %>%
  mutate(
    Lead_Core = sprintf("$%.2f", Lead_Core),
    Lead_Free = sprintf("$%.2f", Lead_Free),
    premium   = ifelse(premium >= 0, sprintf("+$%.2f", premium), sprintf("-$%.2f", abs(premium)))
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Caliber = caliber,
    `Lead-Core (\\$/rd)` = Lead_Core,
    `Lead-Free (\\$/rd)` = Lead_Free,
    `Lead-Free Premium` = premium
  )

kable(
  formatted_table,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
  longtable = FALSE,
  caption = "Median Ammunition Pricing Comparison by Caliber")
```

The table highlights that entry costs depend heavily on the caliber itself. Historically popular cartridges like .243 Win, .308 Win, .270 and .30-06 Springfield - as well as more recent offerings including 6.5 Creedmoor - remain the most affordable overall, with the median price of lead-free loads around $2.50 per round.

## Market Availability & Distinct Offerings

```{r deduplication}
# Deduplicate on distinct products across all stores
unique_ammo <- ammo %>%
  filter(
    !str_detect(coalesce(name, ""), regex("FMJ|Full Metal", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  mutate(dedup_id = coalesce(upc, mpn, name)) %>%
  distinct(dedup_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

availability_data <- unique_ammo %>%
  group_by(caliber, category) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(caliber) %>%
  mutate(total_count = sum(count)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(caliber = reorder(caliber, total_count))
```

### Overall Distinct Products Available

```{r availability-plot}
p_availability <- ggplot(availability_data, aes(x = count, y = caliber, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = ifelse(count > 10, count, "")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Ammunition Type",
    values = c("Lead-Core" = "#2b5c8f", "Lead-Free" = "#d95f02")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Market Availability: Distinct Products by Caliber",
    subtitle = "Unique hunting round product offerings (deduplicated across retailers)",
    x = "Distinct Products Available",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Scraped Retail Ammunition Data From Major Colorado Retailers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

p_availability
```

**How to read this chart:**

* **Bar Length:** The total length shows the approximate number of distinct factory choices a consumer has for that caliber.
  * *Note on data:* While offerings have been deduplicated using universal product codes (UPC) and manufacturer part numbers (MPN), minor overlap may persist due to variations in how individual retailers catalog products.
* **Color Split:** Each bar is divided into **Lead-Core (blue)** and **Lead-Free (orange)** segments, illustrating the relative product diversity between the two bullet types.

**Takeaway:** Choice is heavily concentrated in a handful of calibers. The .308 Win, 6.5 Creedmoor, and .30-06 Springfield calibers represent the vast majority of retail variety. While lead-free options are available in every key hunting caliber, they generally represent 15% to 25% of total product variety, with some calibers like .300 WSM and 7mm-08 Rem offering fewer than 15 unique non-lead loads.

## Retailer-Level Availability

This section evaluates availability across individual storefronts - showing whether a hunter walking into a specific store or ordering from a specific retailer can reasonably expect to find lead-free choices.

```{r retailer-availability-table}
retailer_caliber_summary <- ammo %>%
  filter(!is.na(retailer), !is.na(caliber), !is.na(category), !is.na(ppr), ppr > 0) %>%
  group_by(caliber, retailer, category) %>%
  summarise(
    count  = n(),
    min    = min(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    max    = max(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(category = ifelse(category == "Lead-Core", "lc", "lf")) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = category,
    values_from = c(count, min, median, max),
    names_glue = "{category}_{.value}"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    lc_count    = coalesce(lc_count, 0L),
    lf_count    = coalesce(lf_count, 0L),
    total_count = lc_count + lf_count
  ) %>%
  arrange(caliber, retailer) %>%
  mutate(caliber = factor(caliber, levels = unique(caliber)))

# Determine a single global ceiling for all count bars
global_max <- max(retailer_caliber_summary$total_count, na.rm = TRUE)

# Build bar helper directly in cell_spec or clean inline CSS
bar_cell <- function(x, color, max_val = global_max, max_px = 80) {
  w_px <- pmax(round(max_px * (x / max_val)), 2)
  sprintf(
    '<div style="display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px;"><span style="display:inline-block; width:24px; text-align:left;">%d</span><span style="display:inline-block; height:12px; border-radius:2px; background-color:%s; width:%dpx;"></span></div>',
    x, color, w_px
  )
}

table_df <- retailer_caliber_summary %>%
  mutate(
    total_bar = bar_cell(total_count, "#d3d3d3"),
    lc_bar    = bar_cell(lc_count, "#a6c8e0"),
    lf_bar    = bar_cell(lf_count, "#f4b680"),
    lc_min    = ifelse(is.na(lc_min), "—", sprintf("$%.2f", lc_min)),
    lc_median = ifelse(is.na(lc_median), "—", sprintf("$%.2f", lc_median)),
    lc_max    = ifelse(is.na(lc_max), "—", sprintf("$%.2f", lc_max)),
    lf_min    = ifelse(is.na(lf_min), "—", sprintf("$%.2f", lf_min)),
    lf_median = ifelse(is.na(lf_median), "—", sprintf("$%.2f", lf_median)),
    lf_max    = ifelse(is.na(lf_max), "—", sprintf("$%.2f", lf_max))
  ) %>%
  select(
    retailer, total_bar,
    lc_bar, lc_min, lc_median, lc_max,
    lf_bar, lf_min, lf_median, lf_max
  )

kable(
  table_df,
  format = "html",
  escape = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Retailer", "Total Options", rep(c("Count", "Min", "Median", "Max"), 2)),
  align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "l", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Ammunition Pricing and Availability by Caliber and Retailer"
) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = TRUE, font_size = 13) %>%
  add_header_above(
    c(" " = 2, "Lead-Core (USD/rd)" = 4, "Lead-Free (USD/rd)" = 4),
    escape = FALSE
  ) %>%
  pack_rows(index = table(retailer_caliber_summary$caliber))
```

```{r interactive-product-table}
library(DT)

# 1. Prepare product listings
dt_ammo <- ammo %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(retailer),
    !is.na(caliber),
    !is.na(category),
    !is.na(ppr),
    ppr > 0
  ) %>%
  select(
    Retailer       = retailer,
    Caliber        = caliber,
    Category       = category,
    `Product Name` = name,
    Price          = price,
    Quantity       = qty,
    `Price / Round`= ppr
  )

# 2. Render interactive DataTable
datatable(
  dt_ammo,
  filter = "top", # Adds dropdown/range filter inputs at top of columns
  rownames = FALSE,
  extensions = c("Buttons"),
  options = list(
    pageLength = 25,
    lengthMenu = c(10, 25, 50, 100),
    autoWidth = TRUE,
    initComplete = JS(
      "function(settings, json) {",
      "$(this.api().table().container()).css({'font-size': '12px'});",
      "}"
    ),
    dom = "Bfrtip",
    buttons = c("csv", "excel"),
    order = list(list(1, "asc"), list(0, "asc")), # Default sort: Caliber, then Retailer
    columnDefs = list(
      list(className = "dt-left", targets = c(0, 1, 2, 3)),
      list(className = "dt-right", targets = c(4, 5, 6))
    )
  )
) %>%
  formatCurrency(columns = c("Price", "Price / Round"), currency = "$", digits = 2) %>%
  formatRound(columns = "Quantity", digits = 0)
```

### Availability: Lead vs. Lead-Free by Retailer

```{r retailer-breadth-plot, fig.height=9}
 retailer_caliber_counts <- ammo %>%
  filter(!is.na(retailer), !is.na(caliber)) %>%
  group_by(retailer, caliber, category) %>%
  summarise(options_count = n(), .groups = "drop") 

retailer_caliber_counts %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = retailer, y = options_count, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(preserve = "single"), width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ caliber, scales = "fixed") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Ammunition Type",
    values = c("Lead-Core" = "#2b5c8f", "Lead-Free" = "#d95f02")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distinct Product Selection by Retailer",
    subtitle = "Number of hunting round options carried per retailer for primary big game calibers",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of Distinct Options",
    caption = "Source: Scraped Retail Ammunition Data From Major Colorado Retailers"
  ) +
  theme_light(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

**How to read this chart:**

- Each panel represents one caliber.
- The x-axis lists the individual retailers surveyed.
- The height of the bars shows how many distinct boxes of ammunition that retailer has on offer for that caliber, directly comparing **traditional lead (blue)** against **lead-free (orange)**.

**Takeaway:** Retail depth varies widely. While larger sporting-goods chains and online-retailers stock broad selections of lead-core options (often 10 to 30 choices per caliber), lead-free availability at the store level is frequently limited to 1 to 4 SKUs per caliber, meaning hunters shopping locally have substantially fewer projectile weights and bullet designs to choose from.

## Price Distributions: Where Do Retail Prices Cluster?

Summary averages don't show whether options exist at budget price tiers or whether all lead-free offerings sit exclusively in the premium price bracket. The charts below display the pricing spread across distinct market offerings, using unique products with price averaged across retailers.

```{r prep-product-level-data}
# Summarize each unique product across retailers to its average market price
product_level_ammo <- ammo %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(category),
    !is.na(ppr),
    ppr > 0,
    ppr <= 7.00,
    caliber %in% key_calibers
  ) %>%
  group_by(dedup_id, caliber, category) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_ppr      = mean(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_ppr   = median(ppr, na.rm = TRUE),
    stores_count = n(),
    .groups      = "drop"
  )

```

### Price Spread & Range (Box-and-Whisker)

```{r box-whisker-plot, fig.height=8}
p_boxplot <- ggplot(product_level_ammo, aes(x = caliber, y = avg_ppr, fill = category)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = category),
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.75),
    alpha = 0.25,
    size = 1.2,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.4,
    position = position_dodge(0.75),
    alpha = 0.6,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Ammunition Type",
    values = c("Lead-Core" = "#2b5c8f", "Lead-Free" = "#d95f02")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Lead-Core" = "#2b5c8f", "Lead-Free" = "#d95f02")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Price per Round Distribution by Caliber",
    subtitle = "Comparing median prices, middle-50% price ranges, and inventory spread",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Average Price per Round (USD)",
    caption = "Source: Scraped Retail Ammunition Data From Major Colorado Retailers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

p_boxplot

```

**How to read this chart:**

* **The shaded box:** Covers the middle 50% of shelf prices (the interquartile range). A shorter box means prices are clustered tightly; a taller box indicates a wide spread from budget to premium.
* **The solid line inside the box:** The median price point.
* **The "whiskers" (lines extending outward):** Show the typical upper and lower price limits for that ammunition type.
* **The faint dots:** Represent individual factory products, showing market depth and catalog variety.

**Takeaway:** Across every tracked caliber, lead-free ammunition carries a consistent price premium, ranging from **+$0.17 to +$0.50 per round** (roughly $3.40 to $10.00 more per 20-round box). 

Standard hunting cartridges see the largest relative surcharges: workhorse calibers like .30-06 Springfield (+$0.45), .308 Win (+$0.44), and 7mm-08 Rem (+$0.50) require an additional $0.35 to $0.50 per shot to transition to lead-free alternatives. Conversely, magnum cartridges (.300 Win Mag at +$0.17, 7mm Rem Mag and .300 WSM at +$0.25) display the narrowest premiums, as baseline factory lead loads in these calibers already carry premium price points above $2.90 per round. Overall, baseline lead-free options enter the market around $2.35 to $2.55 per round, whereas standard lead-core hunting options remain widely available near or below $2.10.

### Price Histograms

```{r price-histogram-plot, fig.height=8}
ggplot(product_level_ammo, aes(x = avg_ppr, fill = category, color = category)) +
  geom_histogram(
    position = "identity",
    binwidth = 0.20,
    alpha = 0.45,
    boundary = 0
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ caliber, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Ammunition Type",
    values = c("Lead-Core" = "#2b5c8f", "Lead-Free" = "#d95f02")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Ammunition Type",
    values = c("Lead-Core" = "#1e3f63", "Lead-Free" = "#a84900")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::dollar_format(),
    breaks = seq(1, 7, by = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Price per Round Distribution by Caliber",
    subtitle = "Overlay histograms showing distinct product counts in $0.20 price brackets",
    x = "Average Price per Round (USD)",
    y = "Number of Distinct Products",
    caption = "Source: Scraped Retail Ammunition Data From Major Colorado Retailers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
  )

```

**How to read this chart:**

* Each bar stacks counts of distinct products into **$0.20 price brackets** (e.g., $2.00–$2.20, $2.20–$2.40).
* The **vertical height** shows how many unique ammunition choices - with price averaged across retailers - fall into that specific price window.
* **Overlapping colors (orange/brown tones):** Show price tiers where both lead-core and lead-free options share price brackets.

**Takeaway:** Lead-core options dominate product counts at lower price tiers (between $1.60 and $2.20), creating a tall blue wall of budget-friendly choices. Lead-free bars (orange) sit noticeably further to the right and remain comparatively low in height, showing both an elevated starting price and fewer total options to choose from.

---

### Count-Scaled Smooth Price Curves

```{r price-histogram-smoothed-plot, fig.height=8}
ggplot(product_level_ammo, aes(x = avg_ppr, fill = category, color = category)) +
  geom_density(
    aes(y = after_stat(count)),
    alpha = 0.45,
    adjust = 1.2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ caliber, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Ammunition Type",
    values = c("Lead-Core" = "#2b5c8f", "Lead-Free" = "#d95f02")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Ammunition Type",
    values = c("Lead-Core" = "#1e3f63", "Lead-Free" = "#a84900")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::dollar_format(),
    breaks = seq(1, 7, by = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Smoothed Market Volume Profiles by Caliber",
    subtitle = "Continuous price profiles scaled to unique product counts",
    x = "Average Price per Round (USD)",
    y = "Relative Volume of Offerings",
    caption = "Source: Scraped Retail Ammunition Data From Major Colorado Retailers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
  )

```

**How to read this chart:**

* Unlike standard density curves, these smoothed graphc are scaled to **actual product counts** rather than normalized percentages.
* **Peak Height:** Marks where options are most concentrated along the price spectrum. Rather than grouping prices into rigid 20-cent blocks (like a histogram), the curve reflects a continuous, rolling concentration across the data, with the tallest crest showing the price neighborhood where choices are most abundant.
* **Total Area Under the Curve:** Directly represents total market availability—a taller, wider blue curve demonstrates how much more variety exists for lead-core rounds compared to the lower orange lead-free curve.
* **Rightward Offset:** Highlights the price gap between the most common lead price point (blue peak) and the most common lead-free price point (orange peak).

**Takeaway:** This profile shows the dual challenge currently facing consumers: lead-free ammunition is both shifted toward a higher baseline price and represented by a much smaller total volume of options across nearly all calibers.
